## Reasoning
No variance directive available. `threat.py` and `eo.py` both refuse: entry
8994909 has `started_event: 2`, so it holds no GW1 squad and the switch rule
has no gap/sigma to work from. This plan is therefore written WITHOUT the
switch rule, substituting an explicit judgement — flagged as such so the
review can hold it to account.

Position: entering with 0 points against a league whose leader has 12. That
gap is real but it is GW2 of 38. Long runway ⇒ do not buy variance at a
price yet; the trailing-implies-differentials logic belongs to a closing
season.

THE DOMINANT POSITION IS ONE I DID NOT CHOOSE. Haaland is at league EO 1.60
— owned by 5/5 managers and captained by 3/5. I do not own him. That is an
active weight of -1.60, by far the largest single position in the squad, and
it is a naked short. Every Haaland haul costs me ~1.6x those points relative
to the field; a blank gains me the same. This was not a decision the build
step surfaced: `build.py`'s printed leagueEO column showed no Haaland row at
all, and I initially reported a "one player deep" template on that basis.
That was wrong. Recomputing EO directly from picks_1325554.parquet shows a
two-player spine, Haaland 1.60 and B.Fernandes 1.20.

I am choosing NOT to correct the short this week, for two reasons. Haaland is
£15.5m; buying him from this 15 means dismantling the cheap-attacker
structure the frontier was built around, and a cold-start squad gets one free
shape — spending it in GW2 to converge on the field contradicts the whole
build. Second, City travel to Crystal Palace at FDR 4, his worst realistic
fixture in the horizon. If I am going to be short Haaland at any point, the
away-at-Palace week is the cheapest week to be short. This is a deliberate,
time-boxed short, NOT an oversight, and it is the single thing most likely to
lose me this league. Revisit at GW3 with a fresh threat run.

CAPTAIN. Active weight decides this, not expected points:
  C(Osula)       = +2.00   ep 29.3, 0% league EO, NEW away at TOT
  C(Marmoush)    = +2.00   ep 27.0, 0% league EO, MCI at CRY
  C(Cherki)      = +1.80   ep 26.7
  C(João Pedro)  = +1.40   ep 24.3, CHE v BHA at home
  C(B.Fernandes) = +0.80   ep 31.4 (HIGHEST ep) but EO 1.20 — MUN v IPS home

B.Fernandes has the top projection and the worst active weight of the
credible options: captaining him puts me at +0.80 against a field where 4/5
own him and 2/5 captained him in GW1. It is the low-variance play and it
cannot generate separation.

Against that, the minutes evidence — which project.py does NOT model, its
stated weakness — is disqualifying for the two +2.00 options. In GW1:
Marmoush 0 minutes in a City match that has effectively run its course (a
real benching, not an unplayed fixture); Osula 55 minutes, 1 start; Cherki 27
minutes off the bench. Captaining a confirmed GW1 bench player at 0% league
EO is not buying variance, it is buying a coin that may not be tossed.

Choosing C(João Pedro): +1.40 active weight, genuine separation from the
field, and the only high-active-weight option with a secure starting role and
a home fixture (CHE v BHA, FDR 2). It gives up ~7 ep of projection against
B.Fernandes on paper, inside max_ep_sacrifice 4.0 once the projection's
minutes blindness is discounted — Fernandes's 31.4 assumes nailed 90s that
Osula/Marmoush's numbers also assume and demonstrably lack. I am treating the
ep gap as soft for that reason, and flagging that as the judgement call most
worth auditing at review.

Caveat on João Pedro: CHE had not kicked off at snapshot time, so his 0
minutes is "fixture not played", not a benching. His 64% global ownership
supports a starting role. If Friday's press conference contradicts that,
`lock` overrides to C(B.Fernandes).

VICE: B.Fernandes. If João Pedro is a late scratch I want the armband landing
on a nailed 90-minute starter, and accepting the low-variance fallback beats
an unplanned bench captain.

## What I am betting on
ON (positive active weight):
- João Pedro captained, +1.40 — the primary bet. CHE v BHA at home.
- Osula, Marmoush, Estêvão, Ngumoha all at +1.00 — nobody in the league owns
  any of them. If the cheap-young-attacker thesis lands, it lands here.
- Cherki +0.80, 8 pts off 27 minutes in GW1.

AGAINST (negative active weight — the exposures that can lose the league):
- Haaland, -1.60. NOT owned, owned by all 5 rivals, captained by 3. The
  largest position in the squad and a deliberate one-week short, taken on his
  hardest fixture (away at CRY, FDR 4). If he hauls I lose ground to the
  entire league at once. Revisit GW3.
- B.Fernandes, -0.20 — held but under-weighted vs EO 1.20. Nearly neutral;
  captaining him would flip this to +0.80 at the cost of any separation.

CHIP STATE: 2/5 rivals (HB-YKBNZK, FC Genius) burned Bench Boost in GW1.
The GW1 leader is 12 points clear having ALREADY spent a chip — his lead is
partly chip-funded and should compress. Holding all chips.

WHAT WOULD PROVE THIS PLAN WRONG: Haaland hauling at Palace, or João Pedro
starting on the bench. Both are visible by Monday and neither is hindsight.
